activity.overview: Decide whether a sample represents its population, and describe how to choose a random sample.

problems.prompt: The student council wants to know the favorite lunch of all 600 students. They survey the 25 students in the chess club. Is this a good sample? Explain.
Describe a way to choose a random sample of 60 students from the 600 students in the school.
Which sample is biased, and why? (a) Asking people at the public library whether the town should build a new library. (b) Randomly choosing 50 residents from a list of every household in town.
A factory tests 200 of the 10,000 light bulbs it made today. What is the population, and what is the sample?
Why do larger random samples usually give better estimates than smaller ones?

activity.subject: mathematics
activity.title: Good Samples, Fair Conclusions
